newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Berlian to propose rights issue-report.
newsitem.headline: Berlian to propose rights issue-report.

text.p: Indonesian shipping firm PT Berlian Laju Tanker will propose a US$100 million rights issue and $300 million asets securitisation, Bisnis Indonesia newspaper reported on Friday.
The daily quoted Berlian corporate secretary Kevin Wong as saying that the proceeds from the planned rights issue and assets securitisation would be used to finance expansion plans.
"The rights issue plan is likely to take a place by the end of this year with the ratio of 1:2," Wong was quoted as saying.
Wong also said that the assets securitasion was likely to take place in 1998. "We have consulted two investment banks to discuss about the plan," he said.
He said the expansion plans included increasing its current 17-vessel fleet to 29 in the next two years.
"This expansion needs about US$1.0 billion which will be funded by loans, equity and internal cash flow," Wong said.
The company is expected to book a net profit of 18.3 billion rupiah in 1997, against its 1996 net profit of 13.4 billion rupiah.
